title: Meta Muse exposes users' personal and business secrets when they share conversations
gist: Security firm Claroc found that Meta's new Muse AI agent put conversation titles in share-link subdomains under cf.metaaiusercontent.com, so passive DNS databases exposed them; one query enumerated 6,800 shared links containing confidential business and personal data. Meta paused sharing after Ars reported it. Goodin, also citing an earlier account-hijack zero-day, questions whether an agent that needs access to most of a user's accounts deserves that trust.

themes.theme: GhostShares: passive DNS exposure of Muse links

insights.claim: Claroc researchers enumerated 6,800 Meta Muse shared-conversation links with a single passive DNS query, because each link embeds the conversation title in a subdomain of cf.metaaiusercontent.com.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Design flaws in AI agents can leak data at scale, which is regulatory and reputational risk for Meta's agent push.
insights.quote: “If you had asked us beforehand, we would have guessed that gathering these would take real effort,” the researchers wrote. “It took one query.”

insights.claim: Putting a title in the hostname makes it discoverable, because passive DNS sensors record the hostname as soon as the intended recipient clicks the link, adding it to commercially searchable databases even though the URL also contains a hard-to-guess string.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Any product that puts user content in hostnames is exposed in the same way, a general class of bug to audit for.
insights.quote: What makes Muse’s shares easy to find is the title sitting inside the web address, where public DNS records it for anyone to search.
insights.locator: Claroc researchers were able to discover

insights.claim: Among a few hundred opened Muse links were a candidate's notes for a confidential executive search with a frontier AI lab, a company's internal revenue review for its CEO, a loan application, a bank fraud alert, a real-estate investor's performance report, and a staff vacation calendar.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Users put sensitive business data into consumer AI agents, so leaks carry enterprise-level consequences.
insights.locator: After opening a few hundred of them

insights.claim: Meta paused Muse's sharing feature after Ars reported the research, saying it is reviewing how links can be discovered.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Meta responded quickly, but reactively, to a basic design flaw.
insights.quote: we’ve paused this functionality while we review this report and consider changes to how these links can be discovered.
insights.locator: In a statement emailed a couple hours

themes.theme: Trust gap for autonomous AI agents

insights.claim: Muse is an autonomous agent that fills out forms, books appointments, makes purchases, and creates documents, and it needs access to most of a user's accounts, which Meta markets as deserving that trust.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Agents that hold credentials to many accounts concentrate risk, so a single flaw exposes much more than a chatbot leak would.
insights.locator: Muse quickly catapulted to one of the top spots

insights.claim: Zuckerberg said Muse was 'built from the ground up for privacy and security' a month before researchers showed its share links were easily discoverable.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: The gap between Meta's claims and what researchers found weakens its privacy positioning with regulators and enterprise buyers.
insights.quote: “built from the ground up for privacy and security,”
insights.locator: Muse, which Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said

insights.claim: Three weeks after launch, Patrick Wardle found a macOS zero-day letting any app on the same device take full control of a Muse account; Meta downplayed it and did not acknowledge that a simple ClickFix attack sufficed.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Two flaws soon after launch point to rushed security engineering and suggest more disclosures are coming.
insights.locator: Three weeks after the Muse launch

insights.claim: Goodin argues that the ease of finding Muse share links adds to the evidence questioning whether Muse deserves the extraordinary access it requires.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Trust problems could slow how fast consumers and enterprises adopt agentic AI, which is key to Meta's AI monetization.
insights.quote: The ease in discovering share links further justifies asking if Muse is worthy of the access it requires.
insights.locator: Three weeks after the Muse launch

insights.claim: Muse quickly rose to one of the top spots in Apple's App Store.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Strong early adoption makes the exposure larger and raises the stakes.
insights.locator: Muse quickly catapulted to one of the top spots
